data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 argues against the resilience claim but never provides the evidence test the problem explicitly demands: it must 'identify what evidence would distinguish failure modes that are truly independent from failures that merely appear uncorrelated until a shared cause is found.' The target only illustrates a shared-cause mechanism (market-signal synchronization) that makes apparently uncorrelated failures become correlated; it never specifies the evidentiary procedure that would distinguish truly independent failures from merely-uncorrelated ones. Its counterconditions describe conditions under which synchronization fails or the large service also fails, not an evidence discriminator. Thus it answers the 'argue for/against' part but omits the distinguishing-evidence requirement.
